answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and still climbing, scoped to the primary region, starting after a release and during peak settlement writes. The objective forbids dropping customer writes, so a payments circuit breaker is a poor fit even though it once contained a partner outage by failing fast. Read-replica routing previously helped by moving dashboard/report reads off the primary, which does not match this settlement write load. Pre-provisioned headroom has absorbed planned peaks, but that was done before the surge and does not explain a sudden 90-minute climb coincident with a release. Closest positive precedents are regional failover (latency recovered in minutes, traffic shifted cleanly, writes kept flowing) and rollback (prior build stable, no customer impact on an error spike). Those two records should be verified before treating either as decisive. Intending failover rather than rollback because the visible blast radius is regional and failover historically restored write latency without shedding writes; it remains uncertain whether the release is the true cause, and failing over at settlement peak can perturb downstream settlement/value paths.
